newsitem.title: USA: TV industry agrees on rating system - report.
newsitem.headline: TV industry agrees on rating system - report.

text.p: Television industry executives have tentatively agreed to a ratings system that will categorize TV programmes based on their appropriateness for children of various ages, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.

Viewers would begin seeing the new ratings on almost all entertainment programmes starting next month, the newspaper said. It added that the industry's plans would be formally announced before Christmas.
The post quoted unidentified executives as saying the new system would be loosely based on the broad categories used by the Motion Picture Association of America for new movies.

The MPAA system uses letters and numbers to indicate a movie's general suitability for young people - G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17 - but does not indicate whether a movie earned its rating for violence, sexual content or some other reason.
Members of the ratings development group told the Post they chose the MPAA system as a model because it was both simple and familiar to parents.

In doing so, they rejected proposals from educators, children's advocates and some TV producers that the ratings be based on programme content - say, "S" for sexually oriented material, "V" for violence and "L" for coarse language.
